raw_response:
Ai, what's there to think about? I've been doing this same thing 40 years. Wheat after maize in October, maize after wheat in June. That's how it goes on this plain.

I got 13 mu or so. Not much. Just me and the old lady — the boy works in the city, sends some money home but don't come back to help except for wheat harvest sometimes. So when the busy time comes I call the combine fellow, pay him by the mu, he cuts and threshes in one go. Can't be bending over all day at my age.

**The wheat** — it's in the ground already, went in around Cold Dew last October, same variety as before, does fine. Before I planted I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15, everybody around here uses that one. Now it's April, green-up time, I'll throw down some urea, maybe a small half-bag per mu when the jointing starts. My neighbor Old Wang uses more urea than me but his wheat ain't taller than mine, so why waste money. I'll water it three times from the well — once now for green-up, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling out. If the sky gives rain I skip one, the electric for the pump ain't cheap. Weeds I already sprayed once in spring. If I see yellow rust on the leaves I'll spray, otherwise leave it. Should get me 400, 420 kg a mu if the weather don't do something stupid in May.

**The maize** — soon as the wheat comes off in June I got maybe five, six days. Got to hurry. Rent the rotary tiller and the seeder from the village, plant hybrid seed — you got to buy it every year, can't save it. Put a bag and a half of compound down with the planter, then when the stalks are about knee-high I topdress urea. Water maybe once, twice if July-August is dry. Spray for armyworm if I see them chewing. Harvest end of September when the kernels go hard. Usually gives me 500 kg a mu, sometimes more if the rains come right.

Pesticides and all that — I just buy whatever the agricultural supply store recommends when I go in. I don't read the labels much, I tell them what I'm seeing and they give me a bottle.

That's the year. Nothing fancy. Same as last year, same as the year before.
